newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on telecom buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on telecom buying.

text.p: Thai stocks advanced further, after posting gains in the morning, and finished the week up on Friday on more heavy buying of telecommunications stocks, brokers said.
The SET Index ended up 15.12 points, or 1.59 percent, to 967.60 points. The SET-50 gained 1.54 points to 74.12 in trade worth 5.26 billion.

"Telecoms was where all the action was today, they are a good solid defensive punt," said Rob Collins, head of research at Asia Equity. "The fundamentals haven't changed. As things now stand the Dow is driving prices."
Collins said the market had broken a resistance level at 958 although volumes, which declined slightly today, indicated that the three-day rally may be running out of steam.
He said investors were speculating that existing telecoms companies may shortly be allowed to expand their revenue generating activities.

Analysts said the possibility of New Aspiration Party (NAP) led government after a November 17 general election also spurred buying since the party was seen as unlikely to carry out plans to liberalise the Thai telecoms sector.
Shares in TelecomAsia, a fixed line and Personal Handy Phone concessionaire said to be closely linked with the NAP, rose 5 baht to 60 and accounted for more than 10 percent of total market turnover.
Among others, communications stock Shinawatra gained one baht to 39.25, and Thai Telephone gained 2 baht to 54.50.
